questions.stem: A student places an iron nail into copper sulfate solution. After 30 minutes, the nail has a brown coating and the blue solution has faded. What has happened?

options.text: The iron has dissolved in the water and the copper sulfate has evaporated
Iron has displaced copper from solution; copper is deposited on the nail
Copper has displaced iron from the nail
The copper sulfate has reacted with the water to form copper metal

questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate solution. The iron dissolves to form iron(II) sulfate (which is pale green), and copper metal is deposited as a brown coating on the nail. The equation is: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu.

questions.stem: Which of the following combinations would NOT result in a displacement reaction?

options.text: Zinc added to copper sulfate solution
Magnesium added to zinc chloride solution
Copper added to silver nitrate solution
Copper added to magnesium sulfate solution

questions.explanation: A displacement reaction only occurs when a more reactive metal is added to a solution of a less reactive metal's salt. Copper is less reactive than magnesium, so it cannot displace magnesium from solution. All other combinations have the more reactive metal being added to the less reactive metal's salt.

questions.stem: In the displacement reaction Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu, which species is oxidised and which is reduced?

options.text: Zinc is reduced (gains electrons); copper is oxidised (loses electrons)
Zinc is oxidised (loses electrons); Cu2+ is reduced (gains electrons)
Both zinc and copper are oxidised
Sulfate is reduced; zinc is oxidised

questions.explanation: Zinc atoms lose electrons (Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e-), so zinc is oxidised. Copper ions gain these electrons (Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu), so copper is reduced. Sulfate ions are spectator ions and do not change. Displacement reactions are always redox reactions.

questions.stem: A factory worker accidentally drops an aluminium tool into a vat of lead nitrate solution. What would happen?

options.text: Nothing, because aluminium has a protective oxide layer that prevents all reactions
The lead would dissolve and aluminium would be deposited
Aluminium would displace lead, and grey lead metal would form on the tool
The solution would turn blue as aluminium ions form

questions.explanation: Aluminium is much more reactive than lead, so it displaces lead from lead nitrate solution. Grey lead metal would deposit on the aluminium tool, and the aluminium dissolves to form aluminium nitrate: 2Al + 3Pb(NO3)2 -> 2Al(NO3)3 + 3Pb. Although aluminium has an oxide layer, it can still react in solution.

questions.stem: A student tests whether tin can displace iron by adding tin to iron(II) sulfate solution. No visible change occurs. She then adds iron to tin(II) chloride solution and sees tin being deposited. What can she conclude?

options.text: Tin and iron have equal reactivity
Tin is more reactive than iron
Iron is more reactive than tin
The results are contradictory and the experiment should be repeated

questions.explanation: Tin cannot displace iron from solution (no reaction), but iron can displace tin from solution. This means iron is more reactive than tin. A more reactive metal always displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution. The results are consistent and confirm iron > tin in reactivity.
